name: ChEBI
rationale: Identity authority for chemical structures, and since 2026-08-30 the source of mode_of_action as well: ChEBI asserts mechanism-shaped roles on the same compounds, and conf/sources.yaml maps 32 of them — chosen because the role names a mechanism rather than a structural class — to ModeOfActionEnum, giving 416 records a mode of action where there were none. That is a RESTATEMENT of a role ChEBI asserts, not an inference from chemistry, which is what separates it from the structural-class map tried and reverted in #47. CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE in the SDF directory, ebi.ac.uk/chebi/about), so ChEBI-derived record content is attributable, not public domain. ChEBI also ships a 3-star-only SDF bulk file that excludes ontology classes by construction; our flat-file path filters for both instead.

name: CARD Antibiotic Resistance Ontology
rationale: Antibiotic molecule subtree, resistance determinants and drug targets. aro.obo/aro.owl are CC BY 4.0 — verified against the arpcard/aro LICENSE, GitHub spdx_id CC-BY-4.0, the OBO Foundry registry and CARD's own download page. Redistributable with credit. Note this is the ONTOLOGY only: card.json is under different, restrictive terms (see card-json).

name: PubChem
rationale: Narrow structure fallback for CARD-only molecules: only CIDs CARD already cross-references are fetched. PubChem CIDs are standardized records, not depositor submissions, so a CID's InChIKey can differ from the structure supplied by a depositor. PubChem is also an aggregator whose annotations retain source-specific reuse terms; this adoption does not authorize wholesale annotation ingestion.

name: CARD card.json
rationale: BLOCKED on licence, not on value. CARD's terms prohibit reproduction of non-ontology materials by any commercial organization without written McMaster permission, and the academic clause requires the materials be unmodified and credited — conditions that conflict with both harmonization and CC0. The AMR Gene Family / Drug Class / Resistance Mechanism categories live here and are exactly what the mechanism layer wants, so a waiver request to McMaster is the highest-value unblocking action available. Until then the is_a+participates_in walk over the CC BY 4.0 ontology stands, typing 4530 of 4555 rows.

name: MIBiG
rationale: MIBiG 4.0.1 producer/BGC assertions are seeded from the CC BY 4.0 bulk JSON. The first release accepts only active entries with a non-placeholder expert reviewer, converts SMILES to a Standard InChIKey, and joins only one-to-one exact keys. It preserves taxon, BGC, release and record versions, quality, reviewed flag, and a MIBiG-listed reference. The published pre-write dry run found 3 matches, 17 ambiguous structures, 0 rejected eligible rows, and 23 out of scope; bioactivity labels are deliberately ignored.

name: FDA Drugs@FDA
rationale: The official 2026-08-28 12-table archive now supplies 3703 product-level APPROVED assertions on 211 exact structure records. The importer requires an approved original submission, excludes tentative approvals and combination products, and preserves jurisdiction, application/product, sponsor, approval date, and marketing status. Discontinued is a marketing state, not evidence that approval was withdrawn, so it never becomes WITHDRAWN.

name: FDA GSRS/UNII
rationale: The 2026-08-31 FDA UNII snapshot selects an exact single-ingredient UNII candidate and batched GSRS records supply chemical structures. A name or UNII never proves approval: the importer computes the GSRS Standard InChIKey and writes only one-to-one full-key corpus matches. Connectivity-only salt, stereo, or protonation matches are reported but rejected; GSRS provenance is preserved separately from Drugs@FDA status provenance.

name: BindingDB curated records
rationale: The 2026-09 literature-curated export is seeded through exact reported-and-recomputed Standard InChIKey, primary-citation, quantitative-measurement, NCBI-taxonomy, and assay-context gates. Despite its curated-only label it contains 429 ChEMBL and 260 Taylor Research Group rows; all 689 are rejected by the exact row-level Curation/DataSource marker. The accepted inventory contains 177 measurements, 95 target assertions, and 45 corpus structures. Kd alone supports DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET; Ki, IC50, and EC50 remain MEASURED_TARGET_ASSOCIATION and do not establish organism activity or mode of action.

name: ChEMBL bioactivities
rationale: Best assay-attached activity source, and it carries CO-ADD's ~100K antimicrobial measurements (src_id 40) with organism, concentration, medium and detection method genuinely attached. But CC BY-SA 3.0 is copyleft: content can be aggregated alongside, never relabelled, and a share-alike obligation would propagate to the whole corpus. Refused for seeding under the corpus's CC BY 4.0 record licence (#27, decided): share-alike would propagate to every downstream user, which CC BY does not. Second trap: a ChEMBL 'parent' is not a guarantee of one component; GetParent leaves genuine mixtures, all-salt records and organometallics unreduced.

name: Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database
rationale: All 474 antiviral records carry empty resistance_mechanisms because CARD has nothing for viruses; HIVDB is the strongest HIV-specific candidate but HBV/HSV/influenza remain open. The current HTML shell, asset manifest, CMS repository, and public pages expose no database-data reuse grant; the CMS GPL covers software/content code and is not treated as a database licence. REQUEST SENT 2026-08-31 through the official Sierra tracker: https://github.com/hivdb/sierra/issues/40. Response pending. Remains UNVERIFIED and must not be seeded until an authorized answer covers the database content and named endpoints.

name: NPAtlas
rationale: BLOCKED on licence. npatlas.org/about states verbatim: "The Natural Products Atlas is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 4.0 International License" (database version 2024_09, checked 2026-08-29). NonCommercial is incompatible with the corpus's CC BY 4.0 record licence — it would restrict every downstream user of this corpus, which CC0 and CC BY 4.0 both refuse to do. Excellent content for a curator to consult; it cannot be seeded. Compare MIBiG, which closes the same gap under CC BY 4.0.

name: CO-ADD
rationale: The official Privacy & Copyright page reserves all rights, allows viewing/copying only for personal non-commercial purposes, prohibits systematic download/storage, and requires prior written permission for reproduction/transmission. ChEMBL src_id 40 remains CC BY-SA 3.0. No independent reusable CO-ADD distribution was found. A permission request to info@co-add.org is archived in research/2026-08-31-reuse-terms-outreach.md. REQUEST DRAFTED, NOT SENT; response: none. Blocked unless CO-ADD supplies a separately licensed machine-readable distribution permitting modification and commercial redistribution.

name: BV-BRC
rationale: AMR phenotypes carry organism, strain, method, evidence and prediction fields, but roughly 93 percent are computational predictions; a later extractor must require evidence=Laboratory Method and reject every computational row. The website, privacy policy, official documentation repository, and MIT-licensed API software do not grant reuse rights for API data; software licensing is not a data licence. REQUEST SENT 2026-08-31 through the official API tracker: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-API/issues/204. Response pending. Remains UNVERIFIED until an authorized answer covers the public genome_amr data content.

name: BacDive
rationale: BacDive's current site footer explicitly links CC BY 4.0 as its Copyright & License statement, permitting modification and commercial redistribution with attribution. The strain pages/API expose susceptibility data but drug identity is name-level, so exact chemical grounding remains separate work. A clarification request asking DSMZ to confirm that the CC BY 4.0 statement covers API/bulk susceptibility rows is archived in research/2026-08-31-reuse-terms-outreach.md. REQUEST DRAFTED, NOT SENT; response: none. Terms are compatible, but no data are adopted by this issue.

name: DrugCentral
rationale: Approval, indication, route, structure, and target data are valuable for validation, but the database download is CC BY-SA 4.0. ShareAlike is incompatible with seeding derived record content under the corpus's CC BY 4.0 licence. Use FDA data first; keep DrugCentral as curator reference or in a separately licensed sidecar.

name: WHO AWaRe
rationale: Access/Watch/Reserve classification for 258 antibiotics. The AWaRe antibiotic book is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, so its NonCommercial and ShareAlike obligations make it unsuitable for seeding into the CC BY 4.0 corpus; use as curator reference or a separately licensed sidecar.

name: WHO ATC/DDD
rationale: ATC is a distinct dataset from AWaRe and needs its own current terms review. Do not transfer the AWaRe licence conclusion to ATC merely because both sit in the WHO ecosystem.

name: ClinicalTrials.gov
rationale: Trial interventions, phase, recruitment status, dates, and NCT identifiers are useful investigational evidence, not regulatory status. Terms require attribution, current data, processing date, and modification disclosure and warn of international and third-party copyrights. Use as cited curator evidence pending legal review; never infer INVESTIGATIONAL from a name mention or completed study alone.

name: WHO antibacterial clinical pipeline
rationale: Expert-curated antibacterial candidates, phases, expected pathogen activity, route, target/mechanism and innovation. The associated 2025 report/data use CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO terms; keep in a non-commercial/share-alike sidecar or curator workflow, not the main CC BY 4.0 corpus.

name: ChEBI entry citations
rationale: Already extracted into a citations column that nothing reads. A ChEBI entry's references support the COMPOUND, not necessarily an antimicrobial claim about it, so seeding them into evidence needs a stated rule first.

name: LOTUS
rationale: CC0 natural-product structure-organism-reference occurrences distributed through Wikidata. Follow MIBiG and measure incremental coverage. An occurrence in a taxon does not necessarily mean biosynthetic production, so populate producer_organisms only when the cited source explicitly supports production; otherwise a separate occurrence field is needed.

name: COCONUT
rationale: COCONUT describes the curated collection as CC0, but its terms also preserve original data-owner rights. A whole-dataset CC0 label is therefore insufficient for aggregated upstream rows. Preserve source-level provenance and exclude rows without compatible source terms before considering adoption.

name: Norine
rationale: Nonribosomal peptides with monomer-level representation. Sharpened by a verified finding: the Standard InChIKey does not recognise some 1,5 keto-enol tautomers as the same compound, cannot express cis/trans in organometallics, and does not support relative stereochemistry — all live risks for macrocyclic peptides, where our identity model keys on exactly that hash.

name: ClassyFire and NPClassifier
rationale: Computed structural classes would give structural_class to the records CARD does not cover. Computed, not asserted, so it needs its own provenance marker.

name: antiSMASH database
rationale: Predicted clusters across sequenced genomes. Predictions are not evidence of production; useful for leads, not for seeding.

name: MEGARes
rationale: Resistance gene database assembled from CARD, ResFinder, AMRFinderPlus and other sources. Mixed upstream terms and substantial overlap make source-level licensing and incremental-coverage analysis mandatory before use.

name: NCBI AMRFinderPlus
rationale: Public-domain NCBI software/database of acquired AMR genes and point mutations. Use first as a coverage audit against ARO. Its primary object is a genomic determinant, so do not seed a compound resistance mechanism until determinant-to-drug evidence can be represented without overclaiming.

name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
rationale: PDB archive and APIs are CC0 and can add compound-target complex accessions after exact ligand identity checks. Ligand presence does not prove inhibition, antimicrobial relevance, or mode of action; use as structural evidence only after the target claim is established.

name: DrugBank
rationale: Excellent data, but the licence does not permit redistribution in a CC0 knowledge base. Usable as a curator reference only, never seeded. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: KEGG DRUG
rationale: Same shape of problem as DrugBank: freely readable, not freely redistributable. ChEBI already carries kegg.compound and kegg.drug cross-references, which is the useful half. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: CLSI breakpoint standards
rationale: Paywalled standards documents. A curator may consult them; the corpus cannot carry them. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: EUCAST breakpoint tables
rationale: Current XLS/PDF tables provide versioned clinical interpretation thresholds, not measured MIC observations. EUCAST allows reuse with attribution but prohibits resale, which is incompatible with unrestricted commercial redistribution of the corpus. Keep in a versioned standards sidecar or curator tooling.

name: Discovery and review literature
rationale: Present so the gap is visible rather than absent. causal_graphs is 0% and is the thing this repository exists to hold, but it is not ingestible from any database: a mechanism graph is curator-authored from primary literature, one compound at a time, with every edge carrying its own citation. Listed as REFERENCE to record that no source will close this column and the work belongs in NEXT_TASKS, not here.
